subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All birds can fly. Pigeons are birds. Conclusion I: Pigeons can fly. Conclusion II: Some birds are pigeons. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Both Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: From 'All birds can fly' and 'Pigeons are birds', it directly follows that Pigeons can fly (I). Since Pigeons are birds, at least some birds are pigeons (II). Both conclusions logically follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are lawyers. Conclusion I: Some doctors are lawyers. Conclusion II: All lawyers are doctors. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Since some doctors are teachers and all teachers are lawyers, those doctors who are teachers must also be lawyers — so Conclusion I follows. However, not all lawyers need to be doctors; the statement only says some doctors are teachers, not the reverse. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All mangoes are fruits. All fruits are healthy. Conclusion I: All mangoes are healthy. Conclusion II: Some healthy things are mangoes. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Both Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: All mangoes are fruits and all fruits are healthy, so all mangoes are healthy (I follows). Since mangoes are healthy, it is also true that some healthy things are mangoes (II follows). Both conclusions are valid.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No cat is a dog. Some dogs are animals. Conclusion I: No cat is an animal. Conclusion II: Some animals are not cats. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: We cannot conclude that no cat is an animal just because no cat is a dog — cats may still be animals through another path. Conclusion I does not follow. However, since some dogs are animals and no cat is a dog, those dogs-that-are-animals are definitely not cats. So some animals are not cats (Conclusion II follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All pens are pencils. No pencil is a marker. Conclusion I: No pen is a marker. Conclusion II: Some markers are pencils. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: All pens are pencils and no pencil is a marker, so no pen is a marker (Conclusion I follows by universal syllogism). Conclusion II says some markers are pencils, but since no pencil is a marker, Conclusion II is false.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Most politicians are corrupt. Ram is a politician. Conclusion I: Ram is corrupt. Conclusion II: Ram may be corrupt. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'Most' does not mean 'all', so we cannot definitively say Ram is corrupt (Conclusion I does not follow). Since most politicians are corrupt, there is a possibility that Ram is corrupt — Conclusion II (using 'may') is a valid probabilistic conclusion.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All students who study hard pass the exam. Neha studies hard. Conclusion I: Neha will pass the exam. Conclusion II: Neha is a student. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Since all students who study hard pass, and Neha studies hard, Conclusion I directly follows. However, the statement does not explicitly state Neha is a student; she could be studying hard as a working professional. Conclusion II is an assumption, not a logical conclusion.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some engineers are managers. Some managers are directors. Conclusion I: Some engineers are directors. Conclusion II: Some directors are engineers. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: In logic, 'Some A are B' and 'Some B are C' does not mean 'Some A are C'. The engineers who are managers may not be the same managers who are directors. Neither conclusion follows with certainty.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No table is a chair. All chairs are furniture. Conclusion I: No table is furniture. Conclusion II: Some furniture are not tables. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: We cannot conclude that no table is furniture — tables may be furniture independent of chairs. Conclusion I does not follow. Since all chairs are furniture and no table is a chair, those chairs-that-are-furniture are not tables, so some furniture are not tables. Conclusion II follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All flowers are plants. Some plants are trees. Conclusion I: Some flowers are trees. Conclusion II: Some trees are plants. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All flowers are plants' and 'Some plants are trees' does not guarantee any flowers are trees (the plants that are trees may not include flowers). Conclusion I does not follow. However, 'Some plants are trees' directly implies 'Some trees are plants' (converse of a particular affirmative). Conclusion II follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All A are B. All B are C. No C is D. Conclusion I: No A is D. Conclusion II: No B is D. Conclusion III: Some C are A. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: All A are B and all B are C means all A are C. Since no C is D, no A is D (I follows) and no B is D (II follows). Conclusion III: Some C are A — since all A are C, by conversion of universal affirmative (not valid in standard logic unless A is non-empty), some C may be A but it is not a guaranteed logical conclusion. I and II follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some books are copies. All copies are files. Conclusion I: Some books are files. Conclusion II: All files are copies. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Some books are copies and all copies are files, so those books which are copies are also files. Conclusion I follows. Conclusion II says all files are copies — this cannot be concluded since files may exist that are not copies. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Regular exercise leads to good health. Good health leads to a happy life. Conclusion I: Regular exercise leads to a happy life. Conclusion II: A happy life requires exercise. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: By transitivity: exercise → good health → happy life, so exercise leads to a happy life (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II implies exercise is the only path to a happy life, which is not stated — a happy life could be achieved in other ways. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All honest people are trusted. No trusted person is cheated. Conclusion I: No honest person is cheated. Conclusion II: All cheated persons are dishonest. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Both Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: All honest people are trusted and no trusted person is cheated, so no honest person is cheated (Conclusion I follows). If no honest person is cheated, then anyone who is cheated must be dishonest (contrapositive: cheated → not trusted → not honest = dishonest). Conclusion II follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some stars are planets. No planet is a satellite. All satellites are moons. Conclusion I: Some stars are not satellites. Conclusion II: No star is a moon. Conclusion III: Some moons are not planets. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and II only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: Some stars are planets and no planet is a satellite, so those stars-that-are-planets are not satellites. Hence some stars are not satellites (I follows). We cannot say no star is a moon — stars that are not planets could still be moons (II does not follow). All satellites are moons and no planet is a satellite means planets are not in the satellite group, so moons (which include satellites) have some that are not planets (III follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All teachers are educated. Ravi is educated. Conclusion I: Ravi is a teacher. Conclusion II: Ravi may be a teacher. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: The statement says all teachers are educated, but not all educated people are teachers. Ravi being educated does not confirm he is a teacher (Conclusion I is invalid). However, since being educated is a condition for being a teacher, Ravi may be a teacher (Conclusion II with 'may' is valid as a possibility).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some rats are cats. Some cats are bats. Conclusion I: Some rats are bats. Conclusion II: No rat is a bat. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Either Conclusion I or II follows
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Either Conclusion I or II follows
explanation: From 'Some rats are cats' and 'Some cats are bats', we cannot determine whether any rats are bats or not. Both Conclusions I and II are possible but neither is definite. In such cases where neither conclusion is proven true or false, the answer is 'Either I or II follows' (complementary pair rule).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All computers are machines. All machines consume electricity. Conclusion I: All computers consume electricity. Conclusion II: Whatever consumes electricity is a computer. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: All computers are machines and all machines consume electricity — by transitivity, all computers consume electricity (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent; many other machines consume electricity. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Crime is increasing day by day. The police force is not adequate. Conclusion I: The increase in crime is due to the inadequacy of the police force. Conclusion II: Some other cause also leads to increase in crime. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: The statements present two facts — crime is increasing and police force is not adequate — but do not establish a causal relationship. Conclusion I assumes causality which is not stated. Conclusion II assumes other causes without basis. Neither conclusion logically follows from the given statements.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All metals are conductors. Some conductors are liquids. No liquid is a gas. Conclusion I: Some metals are liquids. Conclusion II: No conductor is a gas. Conclusion III: Some conductors are not gases. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: From 'Some conductors are liquids' and 'No liquid is a gas', those liquids-that-are-conductors are not gases, so some conductors are not gases (III follows). We cannot conclude some metals are liquids since the conductors that are liquids may not be metals (I does not follow). 'No conductor is a gas' is too strong — some conductors may be gases (II does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All politicians make promises. Some promises are not kept. Conclusion I: Some politicians do not keep their promises. Conclusion II: No politician keeps all promises. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: From 'all politicians make promises' and 'some promises are not kept', we cannot identify which politician's promises are not kept. The unkept promises could belong to non-politicians too. Neither conclusion can be definitively drawn from the given statements.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All crows are black. Conclusion I: No crow is white. Conclusion II: There are no white crows. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Both Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: If all crows are black, then no crow can be white (Conclusion I follows directly). Conclusion II is equivalent to Conclusion I — it says the same thing in different words. Both conclusions validly follow from the statement.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some players are coaches. All coaches are experienced. Conclusion I: All players are experienced. Conclusion II: Some players are experienced. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Only some players are coaches, so we cannot say all players are experienced (Conclusion I is invalid). However, those players who are coaches are experienced, so some players are experienced (Conclusion II follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No manager is a fresher. All freshers are graduates. Some graduates are experienced. Conclusion I: No manager is a graduate. Conclusion II: Some experienced people are graduates. Conclusion III: Some graduates are not managers. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: 'No manager is a fresher' and 'all freshers are graduates' does not mean no manager is a graduate — managers can be graduates without being freshers (I does not follow). 'Some graduates are experienced' directly implies 'some experienced are graduates' by conversion (II follows). Since all freshers are graduates and no manager is a fresher, freshers (who are graduates) are not managers — so some graduates are not managers (III follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Vegetables are good for health. Spinach is a vegetable. Conclusion I: Spinach is good for health. Conclusion II: All healthy foods are vegetables. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Spinach is a vegetable and vegetables are good for health, so spinach is good for health (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II reverses the logic — not all healthy foods are vegetables. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All diamonds are precious. Some precious things are rare. Conclusion I: Some diamonds are rare. Conclusion II: All rare things are precious. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All diamonds are precious' and 'some precious things are rare' — the precious things that are rare may not be diamonds. Conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II says all rare things are precious which is not stated. Neither conclusion follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No stone is water. All water is liquid. Conclusion I: No stone is liquid. Conclusion II: Some liquids are not stones. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'No stone is water' and 'all water is liquid' does not mean no stone is liquid — stones could be liquid independently. Conclusion I does not follow. Since all water is liquid and no stone is water, those water-liquids are not stones. So some liquids are not stones (Conclusion II follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All poets are artists. Some artists are musicians. No musician is a dancer. Conclusion I: Some poets are musicians. Conclusion II: No artist is a dancer. Conclusion III: Some artists are not dancers. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: II and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: 'Some artists are musicians' and 'no musician is a dancer' means those musician-artists are not dancers — some artists are not dancers (III follows). We cannot say some poets are musicians (the musicians among artists may not be poets) — I does not follow. 'No artist is a dancer' is too strong; some artists could be dancers via a non-musician path (II does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some letters are words. Some words are sentences. Conclusion I: Some letters are sentences. Conclusion II: All sentences are words. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'Some letters are words' and 'some words are sentences' — the words that are sentences may not be the same words that are letters. Conclusion I cannot be confirmed. Conclusion II cannot be confirmed either — only 'some words are sentences' is stated. Neither conclusion follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All apples are red. This fruit is an apple. Conclusion I: This fruit is red. Conclusion II: All red things are apples. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Since all apples are red and this fruit is an apple, this fruit must be red (Conclusion I follows directly). Conclusion II is an invalid reversal — not all red things need to be apples. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: The government has decided to increase tax on luxury goods. Conclusion I: People will stop buying luxury goods. Conclusion II: The government needs more revenue. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Increasing tax on luxury goods does not necessarily mean people will stop buying them (Conclusion I is an assumption). Similarly, the reason for increasing tax is not stated — it could be to discourage spending or for other policy reasons, not necessarily to raise more revenue (Conclusion II is also an assumption). Neither conclusion logically follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All rivers flow into oceans. No ocean is a lake. Some lakes are ponds. Conclusion I: No river is a lake. Conclusion II: Some ponds are not oceans. Conclusion III: All rivers are oceans. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I, II and III
optionD: None follow
explanation: All rivers flow into oceans and no ocean is a lake — rivers (which are oceans by flow, meaning all rivers eventually become ocean water) — actually from 'all rivers flow into oceans' it does not mean rivers ARE oceans. Re-read: 'All rivers flow into oceans' means rivers end in oceans, not that rivers are oceans. Conclusion III is false. Conclusion I: since no ocean is a lake, and rivers flow INTO oceans (rivers and oceans are distinct), and no ocean is a lake, rivers are not lakes either (I follows by transitivity of distinction). Conclusion II: some lakes are ponds and no ocean is a lake so some of those lake-ponds are not oceans (II follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Smoking is injurious to health. Ramesh smokes. Conclusion I: Ramesh will fall ill. Conclusion II: Smoking should be banned. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: The statement says smoking is injurious to health, but it does not guarantee Ramesh WILL fall ill — it is a risk, not a certainty (Conclusion I does not follow). Conclusion II introduces a policy recommendation not implied by the statement (Conclusion II does not follow). Neither follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All educated people read newspapers. Conclusion I: Some newspaper readers are educated. Conclusion II: Those who read newspapers are educated. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: If all educated people read newspapers, then some newspaper readers must be educated people (Conclusion I follows by conversion of a universal affirmative to a particular affirmative). However, not all newspaper readers need to be educated — uneducated people may also read newspapers (Conclusion II does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some scientists are doctors. No doctor is an engineer. All engineers are technicians. Conclusion I: Some scientists are not engineers. Conclusion II: No doctor is a technician. Conclusion III: Some technicians are engineers. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: All three follow
optionD: I only
explanation: Some scientists are doctors and no doctor is an engineer — those scientist-doctors are not engineers, so some scientists are not engineers (I follows). 'No doctor is an engineer' and 'all engineers are technicians' — doctors may still be technicians through another path, so we cannot say no doctor is a technician (II does not follow). Since all engineers are technicians, some technicians are engineers (by conversion — III follows).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Most students who study regularly get good grades. Priya gets good grades. Conclusion I: Priya studies regularly. Conclusion II: Priya may study regularly. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Getting good grades does not confirm Priya studies regularly — she could achieve good grades through talent or other means. Conclusion I is an invalid inference. Conclusion II expresses a possibility which is valid. Conclusion II follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All trains are vehicles. Some vehicles are buses. All buses have wheels. Conclusion I: All trains have wheels. Conclusion II: Some vehicles have wheels. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All trains are vehicles' and 'some vehicles are buses' — the buses (which all have wheels) are among vehicles, so some vehicles have wheels (Conclusion II follows). However, we cannot confirm all trains are buses (the buses are only 'some vehicles'), so we cannot conclude all trains have wheels via buses (Conclusion I does not follow; trains may have wheels independently but not from this chain).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some chairs are tables. All tables are wooden. Conclusion I: Some chairs are wooden. Conclusion II: All wooden things are tables. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Some chairs are tables and all tables are wooden, so those chairs which are tables must be wooden. Conclusion I follows. Conclusion II reverses the logic of 'all tables are wooden' — not all wooden things need to be tables. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No fish is a mammal. All dolphins are mammals. Some sea creatures are dolphins. Conclusion I: No fish is a dolphin. Conclusion II: Some sea creatures are mammals. Conclusion III: Some sea creatures are fish. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: All three follow
optionD: I only
explanation: No fish is a mammal and all dolphins are mammals — dolphins are mammals and since no fish is a mammal, no fish is a dolphin (I follows). Some sea creatures are dolphins and all dolphins are mammals, so those sea creature-dolphins are mammals — some sea creatures are mammals (II follows). There is no basis to conclude some sea creatures are fish from the given statements (III does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All leaders are visionary. Conclusion I: Visionary people are leaders. Conclusion II: Some visionary people are leaders. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All leaders are visionary' means leaders are a subset of visionary people. Converting a universal affirmative gives a particular affirmative: some visionary people are leaders (Conclusion II follows). Conclusion I says ALL visionary people are leaders which is a reversal not supported by the statement.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Reading improves vocabulary. A rich vocabulary helps in communication. Conclusion I: Reading helps in communication. Conclusion II: Good communication requires reading. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: By chaining: reading → improved vocabulary → better communication. So reading helps in communication (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II says good communication REQUIRES reading, implying reading is the only way — this is not stated. Other ways to improve communication may exist. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All plastics are polymers. Some polymers are biodegradable. No biodegradable material is harmful. Conclusion I: Some plastics are biodegradable. Conclusion II: Some polymers are not harmful. Conclusion III: No plastic is harmful. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: II and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: 'All plastics are polymers' and 'some polymers are biodegradable' — the biodegradable polymers may or may not be plastics (Conclusion I does not follow). 'Some polymers are biodegradable' and 'no biodegradable material is harmful' — those biodegradable polymers are not harmful, so some polymers are not harmful (Conclusion II follows). We cannot say no plastic is harmful since only some polymers are biodegradable — many plastics may be non-biodegradable and harmful (Conclusion III does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All failures are due to lack of hard work. Raj failed. Conclusion I: Raj did not work hard. Conclusion II: Raj should work harder in the future. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: All failures are due to lack of hard work and Raj failed, so Raj did not work hard (Conclusion I follows by direct application). Conclusion II is a recommendation or advice, not a logical conclusion from the statement. Conclusion II does not follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All software engineers know programming. Some programmers work remotely. Conclusion I: Some software engineers work remotely. Conclusion II: All those who know programming are software engineers. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All software engineers know programming' and 'some programmers work remotely' — the programmers who work remotely may not be software engineers (they could be other types of programmers). Conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II is a reversal — knowing programming does not make one a software engineer. Neither follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Coffee keeps people awake. Rohit drank coffee. Conclusion I: Rohit will be awake. Conclusion II: Rohit will not sleep. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Both Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: Coffee keeps people awake and Rohit drank coffee, so Rohit will be kept awake (Conclusion I follows). Being awake means not sleeping, so Conclusion II follows as well. Both are essentially expressing the same outcome and both logically follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Some ambitious people are successful. All successful people are wealthy. No wealthy person is unhappy. Conclusion I: Some ambitious people are wealthy. Conclusion II: Some ambitious people are not unhappy. Conclusion III: All successful people are happy. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: Some ambitious people are successful and all successful people are wealthy — those ambitious-successful people are wealthy (I follows). Those ambitious people who are wealthy (via success) are not unhappy (since no wealthy person is unhappy) — some ambitious people are not unhappy (II follows). All successful people are wealthy and no wealthy person is unhappy, so all successful people are not unhappy, meaning all successful people are happy (III follows). All three conclusions follow.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: Punctual employees are valued by employers. Meena is valued by her employer. Conclusion I: Meena is punctual. Conclusion II: Meena is a good employee. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Being valued does not confirm Meena is punctual — she may be valued for other qualities like skills or dedication (Conclusion I is an invalid reversal). Conclusion II introduces the idea of being a 'good employee' which is not directly stated anywhere. Neither conclusion follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All mobiles are electronic devices. Some electronic devices need charging. Conclusion I: Some mobiles need charging. Conclusion II: All electronic devices are mobiles. Which conclusion(s) follow?
optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
answer: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: 'All mobiles are electronic devices' and 'some electronic devices need charging' — the electronic devices that need charging may not be mobiles (they could be other electronics). Conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II is a reversal and is clearly false. Neither conclusion follows.

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: All pilots are trained. All trained people are disciplined. Some disciplined people are brave. Conclusion I: All pilots are disciplined. Conclusion II: Some brave people are disciplined. Conclusion III: Some pilots are brave. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and III only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: All pilots are trained and all trained are disciplined — all pilots are disciplined (I follows). Some disciplined people are brave directly implies some brave people are disciplined (II follows by conversion). We cannot say some pilots are brave — the brave disciplined people may not be pilots (III does not follow).

subject: Statements & Conclusions
question: Statement: No exam is easy. Some competitive exams are tough. All tough things require preparation. Conclusion I: All competitive exams require preparation. Conclusion II: No easy thing is an exam. Conclusion III: Some competitive exams require preparation. Which conclusions follow?
optionC: I and II only
optionD: All three follow
explanation: 'No exam is easy' directly implies 'no easy thing is an exam' (by conversion of a universal negative — II follows). 'Some competitive exams are tough' and 'all tough things require preparation' — those tough competitive exams require preparation, so some competitive exams require preparation (III follows). We cannot say ALL competitive exams require preparation — only 'some' competitive exams are described as tough (I does not follow).
